# Access, Input and Localization QA: Getting Started

Check whether players can navigate, read and control your game across supported inputs, languages and accessibility settings. This works for any genre: a puzzle game, a platformer, a strategy game, a racing game or a story game all have menus, text, sounds and controls to check.

If `engine/lens.mjs`, `engine/lens-kit.mjs` or `fixtures/good-pack.json` are not on disk yet, write them byte for byte from the `access-input-localization-lens-engine` skill first (Node 18+, no dependencies).

## Words used here

- **Evidence pack:** one JSON file with the measurements for one build. The engine grades it.
- **Game profile (`pack.profile`):** the owner's settings: devices, required tasks and limits. Thresholds live here, never in the engine.
- **Journey task:** something every player must be able to do, such as open the pause menu or finish a level.
- **Approved profile:** a rubric variant the owner chooses on purpose. This template has two: `single-language`, for a release in one language, and `single-input`, for a game with one input method. Both can be selected.
- **Release blocker:** a measured problem that stops release whatever the score. Here: flashing above the safety limit.
- **Case and receipt:** a case is one item the owner approved for checking, listed in `profile.cases`. A receipt is the matching row under `receipts` that records what was run, on which build, and what happened.
- **U (UNMEASURED), N/A and NOT_RUN:** U means no evidence yet (0 points, not a defect). N/A means the approved profile leaves the line out. NOT_RUN means a test was planned but did not run.

## 1. Onboard one question at a time

Ask one question at a time, wait for the answer, then ask the next. Never stack questions in one message. Start from the profile in `fixtures/good-pack.json` and replace each sample value with the owner's answer.

1. "Which game are we working on? Tell me its name, genre and platforms." Then ask: "Which build should I check first?" Then ask: "Where will the evidence come from: a CI run or a manual capture?"
2. "Which input devices does your game support? For example touch, gamepad, keyboard and mouse, or a switch device." Store the answer as `devices`.
3. "Does your game support only one input method, so there is nothing to remap or switch?" If so, we use the `single-input` profile once the owner approves it: `input:2` (remapping, prompts and device switching) reads N/A and `input:1` is worth 20 points. Leave `remap` and `receipts.navigationRecovery` out of the pack.
4. "Which tasks must every player be able to finish with each of those inputs? Think of the path from starting the game to playing and back: the title screen, settings, the pause menu, one core play task and saving or seeing results." Store the answer as `journeyTasks`. The worked example's `title-screen`, `core-play`, `results` and `play-again` come from one synthetic online game; use your own task names.
5. "What is the smallest text size you will accept, in pixels on your smallest supported screen, and the lowest text contrast? Many teams use a 4.5 to 1 contrast ratio as a starting point; that is an example, not a default." Store the answers as `minTextPx` and `minContrast`.
6. "How different must two colours that carry meaning stay for players with colour-vision differences? This is a colour difference score called delta E; the worked example uses 12 as a sample." Store the answer as `minCvdDeltaE`.
7. "Which flash safety limit do you follow? Many broadcast and platform guidelines use three flashes in any one second; take the number from the guideline you follow." Store the answer as `maxFlashesPerSecond`. Tell the owner that flashing above this limit blocks release under every profile.
8. "How late may a caption appear after its sound, in milliseconds?" Store the answer as `maxCaptionOffsetMs`. If no sound carries information the player needs, note that instead.
9. "Which scenes have motion that the reduced-motion setting should calm, such as screen shake, camera pans or zooms?" Store the answer as `motionScenarios`. If the game promises no reduced-motion setting, note that instead.
10. "Will this release ship in one language, or in more than one?" If one, we use the `single-language` profile once the owner approves it; record who approved it, the build and the reason. Under it the locale tests line is N/A and the string inventory line is worth 20 points. If more than one, ask which languages (`reviewLocales`) and which screen sizes (`localeViewports`) to capture.
11. "Who should review my local finding drafts before anything is filed?"

Read the profiles you picked back to the owner and, once they approve, set them before scoring, for example `"rubricProfile": ["single-language", "single-input"]` in `pack.profile`. An N/A line is not U and not a defect, and the verdict can reach PASS.

Before grading a real pack, check that its build and profile match what the owner chose. Record unavailable capture or execution as NOT_RUN. Use the populations (the sets of measured cases) listed by `--meta`.

## 2. What you provide

- An evidence pack (JSON) with `status: "VALID"`, a `liveSha`, a `gitSha` and a `packId` (all three are required), and an `artifacts` list. Every metric group names the artifact id it came from.
- Profile values in `pack.profile`. A missing threshold makes its line U, never a default.
- Anything you cannot capture yet stays out of the pack. It grades U (UNMEASURED), which is honest and costs no false defect.

Metric groups this engine reads, and the skill that fills each one:

| Group | Evidence type | Skill |
|---|---|---|
| `journey`, `remap` | capture | `input-navigation-and-device-switch-audit` |
| `text`, `colour`, `menus` | capture | `readability-and-caption-evidence` |
| `captions` | trace | `readability-and-caption-evidence` |
| `motion`, `flash` | capture | `motion-flash-comfort-check` |
| `strings` | static | `string-inventory-and-pseudo-locale` |
| `locale` | capture (default profile only) | `string-inventory-and-pseudo-locale` |

If part of a line does not exist in your game, never record it as passed. A game with one input method uses the `single-input` profile, so `input:2` reads N/A. For anything no profile covers (for example no keyboard or gamepad menus on a touch-only phone game, for `captions-and-assistive-info:2`), leave that group out so the line stays U, and write the reason next to the profile approval.

## 3. Run the first grade

```
node engine/lens.mjs fixtures/good-pack.json   # worked example, synthetic, not a measurement
node engine/lens.mjs your-pack.json            # your build
node engine/lens.mjs --meta                    # rubric lines, weights and what each reads
node engine/lens.mjs --fixtures fixtures/good-pack.json  # negative and missing-input self-test
```

Read the record: `verdict` (PASS, CONDITIONAL, BLOCKED or INVALID), `grade` and `coverage`, then each line's `level` and `findings`, then `blocking` and `unmeasuredBlockers` (the flash release blocker), then `tickets` (candidate ticket drafts, already deduplicated).

## 4. Report in plain English

- Lead with the verdict, grade and coverage in one sentence. Say how much of the rubric was measured.
- If the verdict is BLOCKED, say so first and name the capture that shows the flashing.
- List U lines as "not measured yet" with the capture that would measure them. Never call them defects. List N/A lines as "not applicable under the approved profile" and name it (`single-language`, `single-input`).
- One local ticket draft per measured finding, with the pack id and artifact ids. Label any synthetic pack as synthetic.
- Rubric lines: input:1, input:2, readability:1, readability:2, captions-and-assistive-info:1, captions-and-assistive-info:2, motion-and-flash-comfort:1, motion-and-flash-comfort:2, localization-readiness:1, localization-readiness:2.

## 5. Skills in this template

- `input-navigation-and-device-switch-audit`: Use when checking that players can finish the game's required tasks with every supported input (for example touch, gamepad, or keyboard and mouse), and that remapping, button prompts, controller disconnects and menu focus all recover. Feeds `input:1` and `input:2`.
- `readability-and-caption-evidence`: Use when measuring text size and contrast over real game scenes, checking that meaning survives without colour, matching every required sound to an on-time caption, and checking that menus and error messages are usable. Feeds `readability:1`, `readability:2`, `captions-and-assistive-info:1` and `captions-and-assistive-info:2`.
- `motion-flash-comfort-check`: Use when checking reduced motion, camera shake, flash safety (a release blocker) and hold or toggle alternatives with paired captures from the evidence pack. Feeds `motion-and-flash-comfort:1` and `motion-and-flash-comfort:2`.
- `string-inventory-and-pseudo-locale`: Use when building the inventory of every player-facing string and the build guard against new hard-coded text (this applies to single-language games too), and, once a second language is planned, running pseudo-locale and supported-locale captures for truncation, missing glyphs and layout. Feeds `localization-readiness:1` and `localization-readiness:2`.
- `file-to-shared-ledger`: Use when turning a confirmed access, input or localization finding into a local ticket draft, or a proposed change to an existing ticket, for the human to review and file in their tracker.
- `access-input-localization-lens-engine`: the engine source and how to run it.

## Blockers to tell the owner about

- Flashing above the approved safety limit blocks release (verdict BLOCKED, grade 0) under every profile. Missing flash evidence keeps the verdict below PASS.
- Capture the player journey on each supported input device; the worked example is synthetic.

Before capture, agree on the case ids and expected values in `profile.cases` (for example the device and task pairs to test for recovery, and the sound cues to match). Run `node engine/lens.mjs --meta` for the required row fields and comparisons. Record one row per approved case under `receipts`, including its id, liveSha and artifact id. A skipped or stale case leaves its line U. The bundled rows and budgets are synthetic.

# Test input and navigation

Rubric lines this feeds: `input:1` (required tasks across supported inputs) and `input:2` (remapping, prompts and device switching).

## 1. Build the task matrix

Take the supported input devices from `profile.devices` and the required tasks from `profile.journeyTasks`. Every device must complete every task. Name the tasks after your own game. Examples (illustrative):

- Mobile puzzle game: `title-screen`, `select-level`, `swap-tiles`, `undo-move`, `pause-menu`.
- 2D platformer: `title-screen`, `jump-and-run`, `restart-checkpoint`, `remap-controls`, `pause-menu`.
- Turn-based strategy game: `main-menu`, `select-unit`, `issue-order`, `end-turn`, `save-game`.
- Racing game: `garage-menu`, `drive-a-lap`, `pause-menu`, `restart-race`.
- Narrative adventure: `title-screen`, `pick-dialogue-choice`, `open-journal`, `save-and-load`.

The worked example uses `title-screen`, `core-play`, `results` and `play-again` from one synthetic online game. Replace them with your own tasks.

## 2. Run the journey on real hardware

Test the complete journey with each supported input, from the first screen to saving or seeing results. Record the device, task, build id and capture for each result, then fill:

- `journey.devicesPassed`: devices that completed every task.
- `journey.tasksPassed`: tasks completed on every device.
- `journey.passedByDevice`: one `{ "device": ..., "task": ... }` pair per successful observation.

## 3. Remapping, prompts and recovery

Where the game supports them, check that:

- controls can be remapped (`remap.remapWorks`);
- on-screen button prompts change to match the device in use (`remap.promptsSwitch`);
- unplugging a controller pauses or recovers safely (`remap.disconnectRecovers`);
- after a dialog closes, the selection highlight (focus) returns to a sensible place (`remap.focusRecovers`).

Set `remap.measuredCases` to the number of checks you ran. For each approved device and task pair in `profile.cases.navigationRecovery`, record a row in `receipts.navigationRecovery` with `device`, `task`, `remapped`, `recovered` and `focusRestored`. For a device switch, confirm the player can carry on with the same task on the new input.

If your game supports only one input method (for example a touch-only phone game with nothing to remap and no controller to disconnect), never record it as passed. Ask the owner to approve the `single-input` profile before scoring (`"rubricProfile": ["single-input"]`, or with `single-language`). `input:2` then reads N/A, never U and never a defect, and `input:1` is worth 20 points; leave `remap` out. If the game has several inputs but one part is missing (for example no controller to disconnect), no profile covers it: leave that check out so `input:2` stays U, and write the reason next to the profile approval.

## Negative fixture

Remove one device and task pair from `journey.passedByDevice`. `input:1` must drop below level 3.

## Pitfalls

- Testing touch with a mouse in a desktop browser and then claiming touch support.
- Checking only the first screen; the journey runs from start to save or results.
- A support claim without a capture. An uncaptured required task stays unmeasured.

Draft a local ticket for a confirmed problem with the shared ledger key (see `file-to-shared-ledger`).

Gather evidence for `node engine/lens.mjs <pack.json>`.

Record skipped capture or execution as NOT_RUN.

# Check readability and captions

Rubric lines this feeds: `readability:1`, `readability:2`, `captions-and-assistive-info:1` and `captions-and-assistive-info:2`.

## 1. Text size and contrast over real scenes

Capture the smallest text and the lowest-contrast states on every viewport in the profile, including text over moving or busy scenes. Measure the rendered frame; a contrast value read from a style sheet alone does not count. Record `text.minPx` (the smallest rendered text height in pixels) and `text.pairs` (the foreground and background colour pairs you captured). The engine compares them with `profile.minTextPx` and `profile.minContrast`.

Examples (illustrative): a racing game's lap counter over a bright sky, a farming sim's crop tooltip over grass, a strategy game's unit health numbers over terrain, a puzzle game's score over animated tiles.

## 2. Meaning without colour

Review controls and important states with colour removed, or with simulated colour-vision differences. Record `colour.palette` (the colours that carry meaning) and `colour.shapeOrLabelBacked` (true when every colour-coded meaning also has a shape, label, pattern or sound). The engine checks how far apart the palette colours stay under colour-vision simulation, as a colour difference score (delta E), against `profile.minCvdDeltaE`.

Examples (illustrative): team colours in an arena game also get distinct shapes; gem colours in a puzzle game also get symbols; red and green zones on a strategy map also get icons.

## 3. Captions, event by event

List every sound that carries information the player needs (`captions.requiredCues`): spoken lines, warnings, a hazard approaching off screen, a timer running out. Match each one to a visible caption or a documented equivalent at the same playback time (`captions.captionedCues`). For each approved case in `profile.cases.cueMatches`, record a row in `receipts.cueMatches` with `event`, `caption`, `eventMs` and `captionMs`. The engine checks that the caption is the right one and that the delay is within `profile.maxCaptionOffsetMs`.

If no sound in your game carries information the player needs, record that decision with the profile approval. With zero required cues the line reads U, never a pass.

## 4. Menus and error messages

Use every menu with each supported input, and read each error message: does it say what went wrong and what to do next? Record `menus.navigableWithSupportedInputs`, `menus.errorsUnderstandable` and `menus.measuredCases`. The first field is named for keyboard and gamepad. If your game supports neither (for example a touch-only phone game), leave `menus` out so the line stays U, and write the reason next to the profile approval.

Record missing evidence locally as a capture task.

## Negative fixture

Swap one caption so it no longer matches its event. `captions-and-assistive-info:1` must drop to level 0.

## Pitfalls

- Measuring text in an empty test scene instead of over the busiest real scene.
- Counting a caption that appears long after the sound it describes.
- Calling red and green "fine" because the shapes differ slightly; check the simulated view.

Gather evidence for `node engine/lens.mjs <pack.json>`.

Record skipped capture or execution as NOT_RUN.

# Motion, flash and comfort

Created by @meta_alchemist (https://x.com/meta_alchemist). Rubric pillar: Motion and flash comfort.

> Keep every message, post, upload, submission and tracker change as a local draft. Only the human reviews and sends, publishes, uploads or files it. Work only on a working branch. Push only when the human asks and only to that branch. Never push to main. The human merges and deploys. Any feature switch you add is off by default.

Rubric lines this feeds: `motion-and-flash-comfort:1` (reduced motion respected everywhere) and `motion-and-flash-comfort:2` (flash safety and hold or toggle alternatives).

## 1. Reduced motion, in paired captures

A paired capture is two recordings of the same scenario on the same device with the same camera: one with reduced motion off and one with it on. Every reduction the game promises (screen shake, flashes, zoom, camera sway, screen effects) must visibly change.

- Record `motion.promisedReductions` and `motion.appliedInPairedCaptures`.
- For each approved case in `profile.cases.motionPairs` (one per device and per scenario in `profile.motionScenarios`), record a row in `receipts.motionPairs` with `scenario`, `normalDevice`, `reducedDevice`, `normalScenario`, `reducedArtifact`, `normalAmplitude` and `reducedAmplitude`. The engine compares the reduced amplitude with the case's `maxAmplitude`.
- Examples (illustrative): camera shake on a hard landing in a platformer, a camera pan across the map in a strategy game, speed lines in a racing game, a full-screen hit flash in an arena game.
- If your game promises no motion reductions, the line has no population and reads U. That is honest; do not invent reductions to measure.

## 2. Flash safety (release blocker)

Count luminance flashes per second in the brightest and busiest captured sequences: level complete screens, explosions, lightning, menu transitions. Record the capture id, frame rate, tested interval, counted flashes and the peak count in any one-second window as `flash.maxFlashesPerSecond`, with a positive `flash.measuredCases`.

- The limit is `profile.maxFlashesPerSecond`, taken from the safety guideline the owner follows. Many broadcast and platform guidelines use three flashes in any one second; that number is an example, never a default.
- Flashing above the limit is a release blocker under every profile, including single-language: the verdict becomes BLOCKED and the grade 0. Draft a local P1 ticket citing the capture for human review.
- Missing flash evidence keeps the verdict below PASS. A game with few effects still captures its brightest scenes and records the measured count.

## 3. Hold and toggle alternatives

Every action that needs a button or touch held down also needs a toggle or another way to do it. Record `flash.holdToggleAlternatives`. If the game has no hold actions at all, record true only with a capture of the full control list showing none.

Record requested hold or toggle exceptions and the owner's reason separately. Under the current rubric a measured missing alternative still fails that criterion. Only a newly approved, versioned scoring rule can change this result.

Level 4 needs all of the above on the supported devices, repeated across the pack's runs.

## Negative fixture

Set `flash.maxFlashesPerSecond` above `profile.maxFlashesPerSecond`. The verdict must become BLOCKED with grade 0.

## Pitfalls

- Testing reduced motion on one device and assuming the rest.
- Counting flashes in a calm scene instead of the busiest one.
- Treating an owner's exception as a pass.

Record skipped capture or execution as NOT_RUN.

# String inventory and pseudo-locale

Created by @meta_alchemist (https://x.com/meta_alchemist). Rubric pillar: Localization readiness.

> Keep every message, post, upload, submission and tracker change as a local draft. Only the human reviews and sends, publishes, uploads or files it. Work only on a working branch. Push only when the human asks and only to that branch. Never push to main. The human merges and deploys. Any feature switch you add is off by default.

Rubric lines this feeds: `localization-readiness:1` (string inventory) and `localization-readiness:2` (locale tests).

## 1. Which profile applies

- **One language at this release:** ask the owner to approve the `single-language` profile, then set `profile.rubricProfile` to `"single-language"` (or a list such as `["single-language", "single-input"]` when the input profile is also approved). Record who approved it, for which build and why. Under this profile `localization-readiness:2` is N/A: it is left out of the grade and never filed as a defect, and `localization-readiness:1` is worth 20 points instead of 10. Leave `locale` and `receipts.localeCaptures` out of the pack.
- **Two or more languages, or a second language planned for this release:** use the default profile (leave `single-language` out of `rubricProfile`). Both lines are worth 10 points.
- Compare grades only between packs with the same profile.

Why the inventory still counts with one language: it finds every piece of player-facing text so it can be checked for readability, corrected in one place and translated later without searching the code.

## 2. String inventory (every profile)

- Inventory every player-facing string: file, line, context (HUD, menu, dialogue, tutorial, results, store copy) and whether it lives in a string table or is hard coded in code. Record `strings.inventoryComplete`, `strings.hardcodedListed` and `strings.measuredCases`.
- Level 3 needs a complete inventory with the hard-coded strings listed. Level 4 adds a build guard that fails the build when someone adds a new hard-coded string. Plant one disposable hard-coded string, run the guard, record `strings.newHardcodedStringRejected` and a `receipts.stringGuard` row (`planted`, `rejected`, and `guardOutput` with the artifact id of the guard's output), then remove the planted string.
- Examples (illustrative): a narrative adventure's inventory is mostly dialogue lines in a script file; a mobile puzzle game has a few dozen menu and tutorial strings; a strategy game has unit names and tooltips built from parts ("{unit} attacks {target}"), which need whole-sentence entries before translation.

## 3. Locale tests (default profile only)

- Pseudo-locale: a fake language that makes text longer and swaps in accented characters, so truncation and missing glyphs show up before real translations exist. Capture it on every viewport in `profile.localeViewports`.
- Supported locales: each language in `profile.reviewLocales` on each viewport. Fonts cover the script, numbers and dates follow the locale, and no essential text is cut off.
- Record `locale.pseudoLocalePass`, `locale.supportedLocalesPass`, `locale.truncations` and `locale.measuredCases`, plus one `receipts.localeCaptures` row per locale and viewport with `locale`, `viewport`, `font`, `truncations` and `missingGlyphs`.

Record skipped capture or execution as NOT_RUN.

Keep single-language approval alongside the profile version. Remove it before grading a newly supported locale. Keep the planted guard output, and record glyph misses and essential truncations separately per locale and viewport.

## Negative fixture

Record the planted string as accepted (`rejected: false`). `localization-readiness:1` must stop at level 3.

# Draft a finding

The shared ledger is the kit's single list of bugs: your own tracker, or an export of it in the kit's ticket shape (`shared/ledger/LEDGER_SPEC.md` and `shared/ledger/tickets.example.json` in the kit). This skill only drafts. Despite the word "file" in its name, the human reviews and files.

Use the project's issue identifier and severity policy. Match on root cause, reproduction signature and build (together, the dedup key). When an existing ticket covers the same failure, ask the owner to confirm the match, then include the template id (`gbf-21-access-input-localization`) and artifact ids in a local change draft.

For a new local issue draft, record expected and observed behaviour, severity, confidence, build, pack id and evidence. Use the fields in the kit's shared ledger example or map them to your tracker. Record who fixed and who independently verified a closed issue.

Examples (illustrative):

- Turn-based strategy: "The pause menu cannot be reached with a gamepad on the end-turn screen." Expected and observed behaviour, the build, the capture id.
- Mobile puzzle: "The level-select label is cut off in the pseudo-locale on the compact viewport." The locale capture id and the string's inventory entry.
- Narrative adventure: "A door-knock sound that hints at a choice has no caption." The cue match row and the trace id.

If you also use Bug Desk (template 18), give it these drafts. It groups the same bug when several templates report it.

An error in a grade or capture belongs in the audit corrections list, not the game bug list. Derive counts from the tracker export.

Gather evidence for `node engine/lens.mjs <pack.json>`.

Record skipped capture or execution as NOT_RUN.
